To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genomes of the thraustochytid strains Mn4 and SW8 are highly similar and lack of a complete gene set of CAZymes and PUFAs synthesis machinery.

the genomes of two DHA producing strains of thrausto-chytrids are similar to each other and possess a third pathway for PUFAs synthesis, and that these strains lack a complete set of carbohydrate active enzymes for degradation of organic materials and are thus likely to be scavengers rather than primary consumers.
we sequenced the genome of two strains of thraustocytrids and discovered a new pathway for PUFAs biosythesis and that these strains are not able to produce cellulosic enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ecological role of thraustoc hytrids in marine ecosystems and their ability to produce PUFAs.

understanding the molecular mechanism of ecological function of thraustocthytrids, and the molecular basis for PUFAs biosynthetic pathways in thraustochydtrids, which will provide a basis for further studies on their industrial applications and ecological functions.
the ecological function of these two thrasutochytrid species, which is a critical step toward a better understanding of their ecological roles and the potential for biotechnological applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thraustochtrids are not just a ‘microbial factory’ to produce PUFAs but also an important member in marine microbial ecosystem.
the thraustochytids are a diverse group of organisms with a broad range of metabolic and ecological capabilities.
the DHA-producing thrasutochytrids have evolved into two different ecological niches, one is a scavenger of marine bacterioplanktons and the other is a detritivore of marine organic matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thraustochydritids are a diverse group of protists with distinct ecological functions and molecular mechanisms for PUFAs biosyntheses.
thraustochtrids are not only important for the production of ω-3-PUFA, but also for the ecological function of the marine microbial food-web.
thraustochtrids play an important role in marine microbial food web, but their ecological function is more complicated than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thraustochtrids play an unexpected role in marine microbial food web and that their genomes contain novel genes that may have potential for biotechnology applications.

the genome of the two thraustocytids strains we analyzed is highly enriched in genes related to signal transduction and motility, suggesting that these strains are highly adapted to dynamic marine ecosystems.

the genome sequence of the thraustochytids is an essential resource to better understand the molecular mechanism underlying the PUFAs biosynthetic pathway, and the ecological function of these organisms in marine environments.
